title: Evaporated milk and water for milk in a dough

evidence.basis: OD-8 (commission 2026-10-11, successive substitutions; ENGINEERING only, not culinary validation, not released guidance; owner confirmation requested). Supersedes v1 (OD-7 B7) in releases published from 2026-10-11; v1 stays in the releases that contain it, and every recipe and cooking session pinned to one keeps it. Ratio, base and sources are v1's, unchanged: 1/2 evaporated + 1/2 water by volume, scaled from the milk's listed total: ATK SRC-CM-38#a-c (tested 75/25, 67/33, 50/50 in pudding, sponge cake, bechamel; only 50/50 close to milk); NDSU SRC-CM-29#e, Mississippi State SRC-CM-30#b, Oregon State SRC-CM-31#d, Illinois SRC-CM-32#a. Disagreements kept: Nestle US 1:1 undiluted (SRC-CM-37, refuted by ATK's test); Nestle NZ 1:1.25 water (SRC-CM-39#a, product-specific). Doughs were not among the tested foods. Engineering bounds 60-480 ML, unchanged. One change from v1: if the milk being replaced carries an earlier accepted change's 'only if needed' extra (cream_to_butter_milk adds up to 30 ML more milk), that extra is carried as the same half-and-half mix, half evaporated milk and half water. That carry is an ENGINEERING INFERENCE from the sourced ratio: no source discusses a hydration allowance. Without it v1 cannot replace that milk at all (it would drop the earlier change's extra), and the engine refuses it.

allowance.stopCondition: Mix it with the same amount of water and add the mix 1 tablespoon at a time; stop as soon as no dry flour remains.
allowance.ifExhausted: If the dough is still crumbly after that, press it together with your hands; don't add more liquid.

allowance.stopCondition: Only mixed into the extra evaporated milk.

consequence.headline: Mix evaporated milk with the same amount of water and use it instead of the milk.
consequence.reason: Evaporated milk is milk with much of its water removed; an equal amount of water brings it back close to milk.
consequence.tradeoff: In America's Test Kitchen's tests a half-and-half mix came close to milk; doughs weren't tested. Use unsweetened evaporated milk, not sweetened condensed milk; the ratio is for US-style evaporated milk, and some countries' products are more concentrated.

proposal.text: Yes, mixed with the same amount of water.
